speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand what might be going on, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or gradually, and have you noticed any vomiting or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your baby had any episodes of forceful, projectile vomiting, particularly green in color, or has he passed "currant jelly" stools? Also, when you palpate his abdomen, do you feel any distinct masses or tenderness in the right lower quadrant?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Intussusception and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound. Given the clinical suspicion of intussusception and the infant's age, we need to confirm the diagnosis with imaging before proceeding with any intervention.

REQUEST IMAGES: Please return the ultrasound images showing the "target sign" or "pseudokidney sign" if present.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception
